Send a capture kept on this computer to the archives later

Source: R/archive_push.R
arcpush.Rd

arccap() keeps every capture on this computer first: the files, their SHA-256, a manifest and, by default, a WARC copy. When the Wayback Machine, archive.rmorie.com or archive.org is down, or there is no network but the source's, the capture is still complete there. arcpush() sends that same capture on later: the very files that were fetched, each checked first against the SHA-256 the manifest recorded, so an archive keeps what you captured, not a new download. Run it again to retry what failed; what an archive already took is not sent twice.

The Wayback Machine takes no uploads: with upload = "wayback" it is asked to capture each address itself, as the page is then. If the page has changed since, its copy differs from yours, and your copy, with the manifest's timestamp, remains the record of what you had.

A manifest with no timestamp yet (the authority was unreachable, or tsa = NULL at capture) is stamped now when tsa is given; that timestamp shows the files existed by now, not by the time they were fetched.

Errors: dir without the manifest.json that arccap() writes, or a manifest that lists no files; nowhere to send (neither item nor upload); as for arccap() for item, meta, upload, reason, tmout and the keys.

Usage

arcpush(
  dir,
  item = NULL,
  meta = list(),
  ak = NULL,
  sk = NULL,
  upload = NULL,
  reason = NULL,
  visibility = c("public", "private"),
  tsa = "https://freetsa.org/tsr",
  tmout = 600L
)

Arguments

dir

The folder of an arccap() capture.

item, meta, ak, sk, upload, reason, visibility, tmout

As for arccap().

tsa

A time-stamping authority, asked only when the manifest has no timestamp yet (default as for arccap()); NULL asks none.

Value

An object of class rmbl_archive_capture, as arccap() returns: one row per file of the capture, with what each archive answered, this time or an earlier one. A file that is missing, or whose bytes no longer match the manifest, is "failed: ..." and is not sent. What each archive took is also kept in push.json in dir, which the next run reads.

See also

arccap() makes the capture; wbsave() and wbrtry() for the Wayback Machine alone; fetchvrf() falls back to the copies.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# capture now, on this computer only
src <- "https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/tbl/csv/35100177-eng.zip"
d <- file.path(tempdir(), "cap")
arccap(src, d, tsa = NULL)
# later, when the archives answer: the same bytes, sent on
arcpush(
  d,
  upload = c("rmorie", "wayback"),
  reason = "Custody table cited in chapter 3"
)
}
